findings.title: deleteMany OR clause deletes unrelated reminders with retryCount > 1
findings.body: The deleteMany query ORs `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` with the SMS-method/scheduledDate condition, but this second clause has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) that happens to have retryCount > 1 would be deleted too, even though retryCount is only ever incremented for SMS reminders in this file. If retryCount is reused/incremented elsewhere for other methods, this causes unintended data loss across unrelated reminder types.

findings.title: Reminders are only deleted on next cron run after reaching retryCount 2, allowing one extra retry/duplication window
findings.body: After a reminder fails twice, retryCount becomes 2, but the current run's deleteMany query runs before the update loop and only deletes rows with retryCount > 1 (i.e. existing reminders from a prior run). This means a reminder that just hit retryCount=2 in this run will still be re-processed in the next cron invocation before being deleted, since the delete step always runs first and would only catch it on the *following* run - meaning the reminder could be retried indefinitely if continually caught right at the boundary and twilio.scheduleSMS is retried for the same booking without respecting the already-incremented retry count the same cycle. This is a minor logic/ordering issue, not fatal, but means a reminder is attempted at least 3 times (0,1,2) not 2 as intended by the PR description ("failed twice" implies deletion after exactly 2 failures).

findings.title: No retryCount increment when message/sendTo is empty
findings.body: If `message` or `sendTo` ends up falsy, the if-block at line 158 is skipped entirely with no retryCount increment and no logging, so these reminders remain in scheduled=false, retryCount=0 state forever, retried every cron run without ever being cleaned up or flagged as failing.

findings.title: No test coverage added for new retry logic
findings.body: This PR introduces new retryCount increment/deletion behavior (on scheduling failure, exception, and cleanup query) but includes no unit or integration tests verifying that: (1) retryCount increments correctly on failure, (2) reminders are deleted once retryCount exceeds the threshold, (3) the OR condition in deleteMany doesn't wrongly delete non-SMS reminders. This is a meaningful behavior change without regression protection.
